literal: Outwardly harmonious yet inwardly jealous—people of the time despised him for this.
idiomatic: Outwardly cordial yet inwardly envious—contemporaries looked down on him for it.

literal: Biao had originally shared an office with Wang Liang; when he went out on campaign he treated Liang lightly, and so came to his death.
idiomatic: Biao had once shared an office with Wang Liang; when he took the field on campaign he slighted Liang, and that was how he met his end.

literal: His second son Gui, styled Yuanqing.
idiomatic: His second son Gui, styled Yuanqing.

literal: In Mingyuan's time he was a Secretariat Gentleman.
idiomatic: In Mingyuan's time he was a Secretariat Gentleman.

literal: Going out on campaigns, he was made staff officer to the various armies.
idiomatic: On campaign he served as staff officer to the various armies.

literal: When Taiwu pacified Helian Chang, he led the generals into the treasury and let each take gold and jade at will.
idiomatic: When Taiwu conquered Helian Chang, he brought the generals into the state treasury and allowed each to help himself to gold and jade as he pleased.

literal: The generals filled their bosoms; Gui alone took nothing.
idiomatic: The generals stuffed their robes full; Gui alone took nothing.

literal: The emperor took gold in hand and gave it to him personally, saying, "You are incorruptible before wealth—that is why I add to your gift: I wish to display integrity before the multitude."
idiomatic: The emperor took gold in his hand and gave it to him in person, saying, "You are incorruptible in the face of wealth—that is why I add to your gift: I wish to show the multitude what integrity looks like."

literal: Later he also served as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and, bearing credentials, invested the Di leader Yang Xuan as King of Southern Qin.
idiomatic: He later also held the post of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and, bearing credentials, invested the Di chieftain Yang Xuan as King of Southern Qin.

literal: At the border Xuan did not come out to meet him in the suburbs;
idiomatic: When he reached the border, Xuan did not come out to the suburbs to greet him;

literal: Gui repeatedly reproached Xuan for lacking the rites due a vassal.
idiomatic: Gui again and again rebuked Xuan for failing to observe the rites owed a vassal.

literal: Xuan feared him and went to the suburbs to receive the investiture.
idiomatic: Fearing Gui, Xuan went to the suburbs to accept the investiture.

literal: On his return his mission was deemed satisfactory; he was made Director of the Secretariat, enfeoffed as Duke of Yan Commandery, and sent out as garrison commander of Wulao.
idiomatic: When he returned, his mission was judged satisfactory; he was appointed Director of the Secretariat, enfeoffed as Duke of Yan Commandery, and sent out as garrison commander of Wulao.

literal: Earlier, when Taiwu was about to campaign north, donkeys were levied to transport grain, and Gui was ordered to coordinate them in Yong Province.
idiomatic: Earlier, when Taiwu was preparing a northern campaign, donkeys were conscripted to haul grain, and Gui was ordered to organize the levy in Yong Province.

literal: Gui ordered that each donkey-owner receive an extra bolt of silk before the animals were accepted.
idiomatic: Gui ordered that each owner of a donkey be given an extra bolt of silk before the animal was taken.

literal: The people said, "Donkeys have no weak or strong—the pack-saddle makes them stout."
idiomatic: The people said, "Donkeys are neither weak nor strong—the pack-saddle is what makes them look stout."

literal: Everyone mocked him.
idiomatic: Everyone mocked him.

literal: He was recalled for investigation.
idiomatic: He was recalled for investigation.

literal: He died.
idiomatic: He died.

literal: After Gui died the emperor said to Cui Hao, "When I passed Shangdang the elders all said, 'Gong Sun Gui as a general took bribes and let bandits go, so that evildoers remain to this day—that is Gui's crime.'"
idiomatic: After Gui died the emperor said to Cui Hao, "When I passed through Shangdang the elders all said, 'Gong Sun Gui as a general took bribes and let bandits go free, so that evildoers remain to this day—that is Gui's crime.'"

literal: When he first came, a single horse and whip in hand;
idiomatic: When he first arrived, he came alone with a single horse and whip in hand;

literal: when he left, a train of a hundred carts followed.
idiomatic: when he left, a train of a hundred carts followed.

literal: Loaded with goods he went south; a Dingling chieftain on the mountain cursed Gui.
idiomatic: Bearing a load of goods, he went south; a Dingling chieftain on the mountainside cursed Gui.

literal: Gui in anger took the curser's mother and stabbed her privates to death, saying, 'Why bear such a rebellious son!'
idiomatic: When Gui flew into a rage he seized the curser's mother and stabbed her private parts to death, crying, "Why give birth to such a rebellious son!"

literal: From below he split her body downward and hung the four limbs on mountain trees.
idiomatic: He split her body open from below and hung her four limbs on mountain trees.

literal: Such cruelty toward what mercy forbids.
idiomatic: Such cruelty toward what mercy forbids.

literal: Gui was fortunate to die early; had he still lived, I would have exterminated his clan."
idiomatic: Gui was lucky to have died young; had he still been alive, I would have wiped out his entire clan."

literal: Gui finally married into the Feng clan and begot Rui, styled Shuwen.
idiomatic: In the end Gui married into the Feng clan and fathered Rui, styled Shuwen.

literal: He reached Director of the Bureau of Rites and was enfeoffed as Duke of Yangping.
idiomatic: He rose to Director of the Bureau of Rites and was enfeoffed as Duke of Yangping.

literal: When Xianwen built a hall in the park, he ordered the secretariat officials to devise a name.
idiomatic: When Xianwen built a hall in the imperial park, he ordered the Secretariat officials to propose a name for it.

literal: Rui memorialized, "I have heard that nothing is more honored than the emperor;
idiomatic: Rui submitted a memorial: "I have heard that nothing is more exalted than the emperor;

literal: nothing greater than modest light withheld between Heaven and man.
idiomatic: and nothing greater than the modest restraint kept between Heaven and man."

literal: Your servant is foolish and thinks it should be called Chongguang."
idiomatic: Your servant is dull-witted and believes it should be named Chongguang."

literal: The memorial was approved.
idiomatic: The memorial was approved.

literal: He died as Director of the Southern Masters of Writing, with the posthumous name Xuan.
idiomatic: He died while serving as Director of the Southern Masters of Writing; his posthumous name was Xuan.

literal: Rui's wife was a daughter of Cui Hao's younger brother.
idiomatic: Rui married a daughter of Cui Hao's younger brother.

literal: She bore Liang, styled Zunbo, clever and fond of learning.
idiomatic: She gave birth to Liang, styled Zunbo, who was clever and fond of learning.

literal: He was Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat and won Emperor Xiaowen's favor.
idiomatic: He served as Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat and won the esteem of Emperor Xiaowen.

literal: Liang's younger brother Heng, styled Daojin.
idiomatic: Liang's younger brother Heng, styled Daojin.

literal: Liang yielded his title to him; Heng rose to Director of Justice.
idiomatic: Liang yielded his rank to him; Heng rose to become Director of Justice.

literal: For separate merit Liang was enfeoffed as Baron of Changping.
idiomatic: For his own separate merit Liang was enfeoffed as Baron of Changping.

literal: His son Chongji inherited.
idiomatic: His son Chongji inherited.

literal: Gui's younger brother Zhi, styled Yuanzhi, versed in the classics, was a student of the Secretariat Academy and was gradually promoted to Erudite.
idiomatic: Gui's younger brother Zhi, styled Yuanzhi, versed in the classics, entered the Secretariat Academy as a student and was gradually promoted to Erudite.

literal: When Taiwu campaigned against Liangzhou, he left Prince Yidu Mu Shou to assist Jingmu.
idiomatic: When Taiwu marched against Liangzhou, he left Prince Yidu Mu Shou behind to assist Jingmu.

literal: At the time the Rouran exploited the opening to raid the frontier; the capital was shaken with fear.
idiomatic: At that time the Rouran seized the opportunity to raid the borderlands; the capital trembled with fear.

literal: Shou greatly trusted Zhi and made him chief strategist.
idiomatic: Shou placed great trust in Zhi and made him his chief strategist.

literal: Zhi was fond of divination;
idiomatic: Zhi was fond of divination;

literal: the diviners all said the enemy would certainly not come, and so no preparations were made.
idiomatic: All the diviners declared that the enemy would surely not come, and so no defensive measures were taken.

literal: Because of Zhi the state nearly perished.
idiomatic: Because of Zhi the state nearly perished.

literal: Later he repeatedly offered forthright counsel and was promoted to Director of the Secretariat.
idiomatic: Later he repeatedly offered blunt counsel and was promoted to Director of the Secretariat.

literal: He died and was posthumously made Marquis of Guangyang with the posthumous name Gong.
idiomatic: After his death he was posthumously enfeoffed as Marquis of Guangyang with the posthumous name Gong.

literal: His second son Sui, styled Wenqing, was Director of the Southern Masters of Writing, enfeoffed as Baron of Xiangping, and sent out as Governor of Qingzhou.
idiomatic: His second son Sui, styled Wenqing, became Director of the Southern Masters of Writing, was enfeoffed as Baron of Xiangping, and was sent out as Governor of Qingzhou.

literal: Because Sui's public legacy was worth recording, an edict praised and recounted it.
idiomatic: Because Sui's record of public service was worth preserving, an edict commended and recounted his deeds.

literal: He died in office.
idiomatic: He died in office.

literal: Xiaowen was at the palace in Ye and held mourning for him.
idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen was at the palace in Ye and observed mourning for him.

literal: At the time every observance was being renewed; Qingzhou's clerks doubted mourning for Sui, and an edict said, "To follow antiquity alone runs counter to the present;
idiomatic: At the time every observance was being renewed; Qingzhou's clerks doubted whether mourning was due for Sui, and an edict said, "To follow antiquity alone runs counter to the present;

literal: to follow the present alone departs too far from former rites.
idiomatic: to follow the present alone departs too far from the rites of old."

literal: One must weigh both paths and calculate gain and loss—the feelings of officials and clerks cannot be indulged rashly either."
idiomatic: One must weigh both courses and calculate gain and loss—the feelings of officials and clerks cannot be indulged rashly either."

literal: The chief clerk said that in recent generations the custom was to wear unhemmed hemp and, once the burial was past, to stop—this might stand as before.
idiomatic: The chief clerk said that in recent generations the custom was to wear unhemmed hemp and, once the burial was over, to stop mourning—this might stand as before.

literal: For the rest, no mourning—a great void in observance.
idiomatic: For everything else, no mourning—a great void in ritual observance.

literal: Let it be permitted that people within the borders wear hemmed mourning for three months."
idiomatic: People within the borders may be allowed to wear hemmed mourning for three months."

literal: His son Tongshi inherited the title and died as Supervisor in the Imperial Secretariat.
idiomatic: His son Tongshi inherited the title and later died while serving as Supervisor in the Imperial Secretariat.

literal: Sui and Rui were cousins.
idiomatic: Sui and Rui were cousins.

literal: Rui's talent was slightly the better, and he was a Feng on his mother's side and a Cui by marriage.
idiomatic: Rui's talent was slightly the finer, and he was a Feng through his mother and a Cui by marriage.

literal: Sui's mother was Li of Yanmen—a family standing far apart in prestige.
idiomatic: Sui's mother was of the Li clan of Yanmen—a family whose standing was worlds apart in prestige.

literal: Julu Administrator Zu Jizhen knew many figures of the north and often said, "A scholar-official must marry well."
idiomatic: Julu Administrator Zu Jizhen knew many notables of the north and would often say, "A scholar-official must make a good marriage."

literal: The two Gong Suns are cousins under one roof—yet when fortune and misfortune gather, the difference between gentry and commoners appears."
idiomatic: The two Gong Suns are cousins under the same roof—yet when fortune and misfortune meet, the gulf between gentry and commoners stands plain."

literal: Zhang Ji, styled Shidu, was a native of Xihe.
idiomatic: Zhang Ji, styled Shidu, was a native of Xihe.

literal: His father Qianqiu was Murong Yong's valiant cavalry general.
idiomatic: His father Qianqiu had been Murong Yong's valiant cavalry general.

literal: When Yong was destroyed, he came over.
idiomatic: When Yong was destroyed, he came over.

literal: Daowu treated him well, made him General Who Establishes Discipline, and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Chengji.
idiomatic: Daowu received him kindly, appointed him General Who Establishes Discipline, and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Chengji.

literal: Ji ranged widely in books and records, was clear in debate and graceful in bearing.
idiomatic: Ji ranged broadly through books and records, was sharp in debate and graceful in bearing.

literal: Daowu favored him; together with Gong Sunbiao and others he served as envoy, was made Gentleman of the Unattached Cavalry, and inherited the title.
idiomatic: Daowu favored him; together with Gong Sunbiao and others he served as envoy, was appointed Gentleman of the Unattached Cavalry, and inherited his father's title.

literal: Earlier, Jin's Governor of Yong Province Yang Quanqi had asked the Prince of Changshan Zun for troops against Yao Xing.
idiomatic: Earlier, Jin's Governor of Yong Province, Yang Quanqi, had asked the Prince of Changshan, Zun, for troops to resist Yao Xing.

literal: The emperor sent Ji as staff to Zun to deliver the reply.
idiomatic: The emperor sent Ji on Zun's staff to deliver the reply.

literal: Ji returned from Xiangyang; the emperor asked him about affairs south of the Yangtze.
idiomatic: When Ji returned from Xiangyang, the emperor questioned him about affairs south of the Yangtze.

literal: Ji said, "Sima Changming is dead; his son Degong has succeeded. The ruler is young and the ministers strong—there is no discipline at all."
idiomatic: Ji said, "Sima Changming is dead and his son Degong has succeeded. The ruler is young and the ministers are strong—there is no order at all."

literal: Quanqi asked me, 'When Wei first attacked Zhongshan, how many tens of thousands were there?'
idiomatic: Quanqi asked me, "When Wei first attacked Zhongshan, how many tens of thousands of men were there?"

literal: I answered, 'More than four hundred thousand.'
idiomatic: I answered, 'More than four hundred thousand.'

literal: Quanqi said, 'How many armored war-horses does Wei have?'
idiomatic: Quanqi said, "How many armored war-horses does Wei possess?"

literal: I answered, 'The central army has more than a hundred thousand elite cavalry; the outer armies are beyond counting.'
idiomatic: I answered, "The central army has more than a hundred thousand elite cavalry; the outer armies are beyond counting."

literal: Quanqi said, 'With that force, to chastise the Qiang—would they not be destroyed!'
idiomatic: Quanqi said, "With a force like that, to chastise the Qiang—would they not be utterly destroyed!"

literal: He also asked, 'When Wei pacified Zhongshan, how many households were moved north?'
idiomatic: He also asked, "When Wei pacified Zhongshan, how many households were relocated north?"

literal: I answered, 'More than seventy thousand families.'
idiomatic: I answered, 'More than seventy thousand families.'

literal: Quanqi asked, 'What city was the capital?'
idiomatic: Quanqi asked, 'What city was the capital?'

literal: I answered, 'The capital was Pingcheng.'
idiomatic: I answered, 'The capital was Pingcheng.'

literal: Quanqi said, 'With such a multitude, what need of walls!'
idiomatic: Quanqi said, "With so vast a multitude, what need is there of city walls!"

literal: He also asked, 'Does the Wei emperor mean to make Pingcheng his capital for long,
idiomatic: He also asked, "Does the Wei emperor intend to keep Pingcheng as his capital long,

literal: or will he move?'
idiomatic: or will he move?'

literal: I answered, 'I do not know.'
idiomatic: I answered, 'I do not know.'

literal: Quanqi heard that the court did not intend to settle east of the mountains and looked pleased, saying, 'Relief for Luoyang depends on Wei; if we can be preserved, we shall surely repay you richly.
idiomatic: Quanqi heard that the court did not intend to settle east of the mountains and looked pleased, saying, "Relief for Luoyang depends on Wei; if we can be preserved, we shall surely repay you richly.

literal: If the Qiang should prevail, better let Wei take it.'"
idiomatic: If the Qiang should prevail, better let Wei take it."

literal: Daowu praised his report, richly rewarded the envoy, and promised to rescue Luoyang.
idiomatic: Daowu commended his report, richly rewarded the envoy, and pledged to rescue Luoyang.

literal: Later, because repeated missions pleased the throne, he was made General of Victorious Troops.
idiomatic: Later, because his repeated missions met with imperial approval, he was appointed General of Victorious Troops.

literal: He died; his son Duoluo inherited the title and was stripped of rank for an offense.
idiomatic: He died; his son Duoluo inherited the title but was stripped of rank for an offense.

literal: Li Xian, styled Rongren, was a native of Lunu in Zhongshan.
idiomatic: Li Xian, styled Rongren, came from Lunu in Zhongshan.

literal: In youth he loved learning and was skilled in physiognomy and divination.
idiomatic: In his youth he loved learning and was skilled in physiognomy and divination.

literal: Murong Yong welcomed him as strategist and urged Yong to hold Changzi city.
idiomatic: Murong Yong welcomed him as strategist and urged Yong to hold the city of Changzi.

literal: He served Yong as Director of the Secretariat.
idiomatic: He served Yong as Director of the Secretariat.

literal: When Yong was destroyed, he was moved to Zhongshan.
idiomatic: After Yong's fall, he was relocated to Zhongshan.
